n: Ryan Park Activity Building — Roof Replacement & Overhang Reframing
d: Best fit on the board. Roofing and framing are two unrelated trades, so your Class B primes it cleanly — no added license needed. Single building, two subs.

n: Begg Pool Deck & Drainage System Repairs, Polliwog Park
trade: Concrete, drainage, fencing, hardscape, landscape restoration
d: Multi-trade and B-eligible, with the most runway of anything actionable. Watch for: DIR registration, prevailing wage, possible prequalification — and real change-order risk on whatever is found under the deck.

Simple and sub-able: 800 sf structure, 10-ft block wall, bollards, vegetation clearance. Decides itself within 48 hours. Only bid it with a demo sub who will price it first thing Monday — demo pricing turns on abatement scope and disposal tipping fees.
Small, clean demo-and-rebuild scope. No mandatory pre-bid, so nothing blocks a new bidder.

Small and simple, no mandatory pre-bid. Even read as a single-trade concrete scope this is primeable — carry a C-8 sub if the solicitation calls for one. Check the stated license requirement, then price it.
Under the $5M ceiling. You would need both a roofing sub and an abatement sub, and the hazmat component is where the pricing risk sits.

trade: Demo of existing cooler + new freezer install
d: Squarely Class B general building scope. Needs a refrigeration and electrical sub.

B-eligible, small, and the pre-bid was optional rather than mandatory — so it is still open to you. But be honest about margin: modular relocation is a niche, the handful of firms that move classrooms for a living will underbid you, and your margin is only a markup on theirs.

Correction — this is biddable. It is a prime contract, and under §7057(b) a Class B may prime a single-trade job by subcontracting the work to an appropriately licensed contractor. Carry a C-27 sub and you can bid it. Routine landscape maintenance is also often let as a service contract rather than licensed contracting work. Check the solicitation’s stated license requirement first — if it names C-27 only, that governs; if it names A/B/C-27 or just a valid licence, you are in. Recurring maintenance with an option year is exactly the revenue shape you want.

n: CSU San Marcos — Blanket Minor Capital Advertisement
d: Register for this — it is free and passive. An open vendor list running through June 2027 for projects up to $1.157M each. This is the same mechanism as a CUPCCAA informal list: get on it once and the work comes to you.

n: On-Call Flooring Repair & Replacement, Palm Springs International Airport
d: Correction — this is biddable as prime. An on-call agreement with the City is a prime contract, so you may hold it and subcontract the flooring to a C-15. Confirm the solicitation’s stated license requirement. On-call agreements are the recurring revenue you want, so this is worth the ten minutes. Price in airport badging, security escorts and likely night work.
Really a supply agreement rather than a construction contract — you would be competing on thin dealer margins against distributors, not contractors.

n: Turnkey GC Services — EV, Photovoltaic & Battery Energy Storage
trade: Class B listed alongside C-10 / C-46
d: Class B is genuinely listed — but the award runs through a statewide cooperative MSA (CFCC, SPURR, CMAS or equivalent). If you are not already on one of those vehicles you cannot bid it, and you cannot get on one this week. Beyond that, turnkey design-through-commissioning on battery storage is a specialty EPC play, not simple work you sub out. Worth noting for later: getting onto a cooperative purchasing vehicle is a real strategy for future years.

Too large to prime, but Erickson-Hall is actively soliciting subcontractor bids. Your landscaping, concrete or fencing crews can bid a slice. Erickson-Hall is a San Diego prime with a heavy school/public-agency focus — worth a relationship beyond this one job.
Same shape as Einstein. Swinerton runs a formal subcontractor prequalification and a supplier-diversity program — get into their system rather than just chasing this one package.

n: JUSD Rustic Lane ES Modernization, Jurupa Valley
d: Large multi-building campus rebuild. Only makes sense as a sub-trade opportunity — find the prime once it is awarded.

n: Otay WTP Switchboard Replacement, Chula Vista
trade: Demo of shed/fence + new fencing, concrete, generator
d: Good trade match and good size, but the mandatory pre-bid was 7/29 and has passed — that normally disqualifies a bidder who did not attend. Confirm attendance status before spending any time on it.
A strong framing and demolition match at a nice size — mandatory pre-bid was 8/4 and passed. Exactly the profile to chase next time; note who wins it.

n: Other expired pre-bids and closed solicitations
d: Mandatory pre-bid already passed: ECC Ceramics Renovation (8/6), Del Mar USD District Office Roof Repair (8/12), Fox Field Relocation of two buildings (8/5). Already closed: El Cajon Weed Abatement, Palm Desert On-Call Court Maintenance, La Mirada Pool Deck Renovation. Too tight to react to: Albert Einstein ES Modernization, San Diego Housing Commission As-Needed Restoration, San Marcos As-Needed Painting, Corona Citywide Sidewalk Phase II, CSU Dominguez Hills Job Order Contract, Santa Monica Painting Services.

n: Padre Dam MWD — Lake Jennings Campground & Public Access Improvements
d: Two independent disqualifiers: nearly double your ceiling, and progressive design-build would require a design team on your side of the table before you could even respond. Notable as the only row in the whole tracker with a hard dollar figure attached.

n: West Hollywood Recovery Center — Log Cabin Renovation & Expansion
d: It is genuinely Class B work, but it is a two-phase multi-building program at or above the ceiling — the opposite of a simple job you sub out.
Far outside your range and complexity.

trade: Requires Class A, or C-8 / C-12 / D-12 to prime
d: Paving, road reconstruction, resurfacing, slurry seal, curb/gutter/sidewalk in the public right of way, and reservoir rehabilitation all require a Class A license to prime. This eliminated roughly 24 tracker rows before dollar value ever mattered, including both Caltrans jobs (11-430884 Ramona, 11-146654 La Mesa), CVWD Whitewater River Channel, Long Beach Harbor Scenic Drive, Solana Beach ADA ramps, Countywide Culvert Repair, Poway slurry seal, San Diego Airport T2 Transportation Island, Troy Street, Presioca Street sidewalk, Buckley Street ADA, Fairmount Park Rose Garden ADA, and Orange Terrace rubber surfacing. You can still sub concrete or landscaping slices to the engineering prime on any of these.

n: Re-open these four — wrongly screened out
a: Burbank, Norwalk, City of Industry, Claremont
d: The Burbank landscape maintenance agreement, the Norwalk fence repair, the City of Industry irrigation retrofit and the Claremont on-call electrical agreement were all screened out as single-trade. That was wrong — they are prime contracts, and a Class B may prime single-trade work by subcontracting it to an appropriately licensed contractor (§7057(b)). Go back and check each one’s stated license requirement and whether the deadline has passed. If any are still open and name B as acceptable, they are live.
